**Sikhae (Seafood Stew) – A Quick & Flavorful Korean Recipe** Sikhae (시해) is a hearty, spicy seafood stew that’s perfect for a cozy dinner. It’s usually made with a mix of fresh fish, shrimp, clams, and sometimes squid, simmered in a savory broth with Korean chili paste (고추장) and gochugaru (고춧가루). Below is a simple, beginner‑friendly recipe that you can tweak to suit your taste. --- ## Ingredients (serves 4) | Item | Amount | Notes | |------|--------|-------| | **Seafood mix** | 400 g | Use a combination of:
• 200 g white fish fillets (cod, pollock, or snapper)
• 100 g shrimp (peeled, deveined)
• 100 g clams or mussels (cleaned)
• 50 g squid (sliced) | | **Vegetables** | 1 cup |
• 1 small onion, sliced
• 1 carrot, julienned
• 1/2 cup sliced shiitake mushrooms (optional)
• 1 cup spinach or bok choy | | **Broth** | 4 cups | Use fish stock or water + fish sauce | | **Seasonings** | |
• 2 Tbsp Korean chili paste (고추장)
• 1 Tbsp Korean chili flakes (고춧가루)
• 1 Tbsp soy sauce
• 1 Tbsp fish sauce (optional)
• 1 Tbsp sesame oil
• 1 tsp sugar (optional) | | **Aromatics** | |
• 3 cloves garlic, minced
• 1 tsp ginger, minced
• 1 scallion, chopped (for garnish) | | **Optional** | |
• 1 tsp Korean fermented soybean paste (된장) for depth
• 1 tsp Korean rice wine (청주) for aroma | --- ## Equipment - Medium‑sized pot or Dutch oven - Cutting board & knife - Measuring spoons --- ## Instructions ### 1. Prep the Seafood 1. **Clean** all seafood. Pat dry with paper towels. 2. **Cut** fish into bite‑size pieces. Slice squid into rings if not already sliced. 3. **Set aside**. ### 2. Make the Broth 1. In the pot, pour in the 4 cups of water or fish stock. 2. Add the minced garlic, ginger, and a pinch of salt. 3. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce to a simmer. ### 3. Add Vegetables 1. Add the sliced onion, carrot, and mushrooms to the pot. 2. Simmer for 3–4 minutes until they start to soften. ### 4. Season the Broth 1. Stir in the **고추장** (2 Tbsp) and **고춧가루** (1 Tbsp). If you like it spicier, add more 고춧가루. 2. Add soy sauce, fish sauce (if using), sesame oil, and sugar. Stir until the paste dissolves completely. 3. Optional: Add a teaspoon of fermented soybean paste for umami depth. ### 5. Add Seafood 1. Gently drop in the fish, shrimp, clams, and squid. 2. Cover and let it simmer for 5–7 minutes. The clams/mussels should open; discard any that remain closed. ### 6. Finish with Greens 1. Toss in the spinach or bok choy. Cook for another 1–2 minutes until wilted. ### 7. Final Touches 1. Taste and adjust seasoning: more soy sauce for saltiness, more 고추장 for sweetness, or a splash of rice wine for aroma. 2. Drizzle a little sesame oil over the top for fragrance. ### 8. Serve 1. Ladle the stew into bowls. 2. Garnish with chopped scallions and a few extra chili flakes if desired. 3. Serve hot with steamed rice or a side of kimchi. --- ## Tips & Variations | Tip | Why it Helps | |-----|--------------| | **Use fresh seafood** | Freshness translates to better flavor and texture. | | **Don’t overcook** | Shrimp and squid become rubbery quickly; fish should be flaky but not mushy. | | **Add a splash of rice wine** | Enhances aroma and balances the heat. | | **Try different seafood combos** | Mix in octopus, scallops, or even a small amount of crab for variety. | | **Make a “dry” version** | Reduce the broth to a thicker consistency for a more concentrated taste. | | **Serve with a side of kimchi** | The tangy kimchi cuts through the richness of the stew. | --- Enjoy your homemade **Sikhae**! It’s a comforting, protein‑rich dish that’s perfect for a rainy day or when you need a quick, satisfying meal. Feel free to experiment with the spice level and seafood mix to make it truly your own. Happy cooking!
